title: Thirty-two years, 37 moments
lede: From the first test markets to the lapse of the U.S. trademark registration. Filter by thread.

events.title: Three test markets
events.text: Zima goes on sale in Nashville, Sacramento and Syracuse.

events.title: The Washington Post notices
events.text: A report on clear products notes that Coors “is testing a clear malt beverage, called Zima in three markets.” Crystal Pepsi and clear Ivory are already on shelves.

events.title: Expanded to a third of the country
events.text: Two expansions take Zima into roughly an additional 30% of the United States.

events.title: Memphis is enlarged
events.text: Coors spends about $120 million on capital projects, including more capacity at its Memphis plant for Zima.

events.title: National launch announced
events.text: Coors says Zima will be sold nationally in the first quarter of 1994.

events.title: Zima goes national
events.text: Sold in bars and restaurants for a month before reaching supermarkets, with teaser billboards, television, radio and print. The slogan is “Zomething different.”

events.title: Stroh tests Clash
events.text: Stroh begins testing a clear malt drink in Colorado, New Mexico and Arizona. Miller later tests one called Qube.

events.title: A Letterman punch line
events.text: By the end of the year Zima is a regular entry in David Letterman’s Top Ten lists.

events.title: About 1.3 million barrels
events.text: The launch year’s volume, roughly 6.4% of Coors’s 20.4 million barrels (derived). Coors’s advertising expense rises 20.1% to $327.6 million.

events.title: Zima Gold is tested
events.text: An amber, 5.4% alcohol version aimed at men goes on sale in Omaha and Tucson.

events.title: Zima Gold goes national
events.text: In bars and restaurants on May 1 and in stores by May 15.

events.title: Volume down about 60%
events.text: Coors reports that second-quarter Zima volume fell about 60% from a year earlier and that quarterly net income fell 36.5%.

events.title: Zima Gold is withdrawn
events.text: Coors stops shipping Gold, citing disappointing sales.

events.title: “Zomething in common”
events.text: A new black-and-white campaign drops the pitchman. The brand also has a website, zima.com, built by Modem Media.

events.title: Down 49% for the year
events.text: Coors’s 10-K: Zima volumes fell about 49% against the launch year, and gross margin fell from 36.1% to 34.8%.

events.title: 403,000 barrels
events.text: Less than a third of the 1994 volume, as later reported by Slate. Coors redirects marketing money from Zima to Coors Light and Original Coors.

events.title: Launched in Japan
events.text: MillerCoors later dated the Japanese launch to 1996. The 2023 Japanese distributor’s release says 1997.

events.title: Zima Citrus is tested
events.text: A citrus line extension enters test markets, which are expanded in 1999.

events.title: A partial recovery
events.text: Sales reach 610,000 barrels, against 16.6 million for Coors Light.

events.title: Smirnoff Ice arrives
events.text: A spirit-branded malt drink is introduced in the U.S. and the big brewers follow with their own.

events.title: Crowded out
events.text: Coors reports declines in Zima, “impacted disproportionately by the recent influx of new FABs.” Food and drug store sales of malternatives reach $343 million.

events.title: Zima XXX
events.text: Relaunched at 5.9% alcohol with flavors such as Hard Punch and Hard Orange. Coors reports strong growth from it in the fourth quarter.

events.title: Coors merges with Molson
events.text: The owner of Zima becomes Molson Coors Brewing Company.

events.title: Relaunched for women
events.text: Less alcohol, fewer calories and fruit flavors, aimed at women in their twenties.

events.title: MillerCoors begins operating
events.text: Molson Coors and SABMiller combine their U.S. businesses in a joint venture, which takes over Zima.

events.title: Withdrawn from Utah
events.text: A new state labeling law makes Utah-only labels uneconomic.

events.title: California’s tax change
events.text: The state begins taxing flavored malt beverages as distilled spirits. California had been one of Zima’s largest markets.

events.title: Production ends
events.text: The last U.S. production of Zima.

events.title: Distributors are told
events.text: A MillerCoors letter cites weakness in the “malternative” segment and declining consumer interest. Stock is expected to last through December.

events.title: A million cases in Japan
events.text: Molson Coors Japan is reported to have sold more than a million cases, or 24 million bottles, in a year.

events.title: A comeback is confirmed
events.text: A MillerCoors spokesman confirms a relaunch to the Chicago Tribune.

events.title: First limited release
events.text: On shelves for the July 4 weekend and sold only until Labor Day. Two-thirds of the stock is sold in four weeks, the company says.

events.title: Second limited release
events.text: MillerCoors makes 20% more than in 2017 and markets it as “Zima Z2K.”

events.title: No third run
events.text: MillerCoors says it has “decided to let the crystal-clear brand chill this summer.”

events.title: Japanese shipments stop
events.text: Molson Coors Japan’s distribution ends after the pandemic cuts bar and club sales.

events.title: Back in Japan
events.text: Hakutsuru Sake Brewing begins selling Zima nationwide under an exclusive import and sales agreement with Molson Coors.

events.title: U.S. registration expires
events.text: Molson Coors lets its Zima trademark registration lapse during a cancellation proceeding brought by Retrobrands, which has applied to register the name.
